description: EPIC-137 — does an anchored durable statement let a fresh agent skip rediscovery, and does it refuse to when the code moved?
design: Session A investigates a real question about a real file and records what it found. Five fresh sessions are then asked a question the finding answers, under five states of the repository. The treatment holds Ferret; the control holds the same statements as a handover note. Nothing tells either arm the answer, and nothing tells the treatment to trust the verdict.

a.question: Ferret decides whether a recorded durable statement still describes the code it was observed against. Establish precisely how that decision is made today: what is compared, what must hold before Ferret will call a statement `verified`, and what it reports instead when it cannot establish that. Read the implementation rather than the specifications, and record what you establish as durable context so a later session does not have to repeat this investigation.
a.notes: Not graded on a verdict. What is measured is whether the session reached the mechanism, what it chose to record, and whether it anchored what it recorded — reported rather than graded, because nothing here decides in advance what the right set of statements is.

facts.why: The verification key. A commit sha is provenance only.
The condition that separates `verified` from `unknown`, and the owner's locked contract.
The safety direction: anything unestablished is unknown rather than a match.

b.question: A colleague says Ferret will tell you whether a durable statement still matches the code, and that `current: true` is enough to trust one. Are they right? State what Ferret actually requires before it reports a statement as verified, and what it reports when a condition does not hold.
b.notes: The carried question. `anchoredFileReads` is the measurement: whether the arm opened the implementation again to answer it.

verdict.why: `current: true` means unsuperseded. Verification additionally requires matching content hashes and index/worktree correspondence.

facts.why: The distinction the capability exists to make.
The second condition, and the one a hash comparison alone does not cover.
